title: Area and Perimeter
summary: Learn to measure around shapes and calculate the space inside them for common GCSE questions.

blocks.text: The area of a shape is the space inside the shape. Area is measured in squares.
### Finding the area of a rectangle
Here is a rectangle drawn on a centimetre grid.

To find the area of a rectangle multiply the length by the width.  
(We could also count the squares but this will not work from more complex questions)
In this example we have a length of 6cm and a width of 3cm.

Area = length × width  
Area = 6 × 3  
**Area = 18 cm2**
The units are cm2: one cm2 is a square that measures 1cm by 1 cm.

blocks.title: Example 1: A rectangle is drawn on a centimetre grid Calculate the area of the rectangle

items.prompt: A rectangle is $9$ cm long and $4$ cm wide. What is its area?
items.explanation: The area of a rectangle is length × width, so $9 \times 4 = 36\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A square has an area of $81\text{ cm}^2$. What is its side length?
items.explanation: The side length multiplied by itself gives $81$. Since $9 \times 9 = 81$, the side length is $9$ cm.

blocks.text: ### Finding the area of a triangle
We can think of a triangle as half of a rectangle
To calculate the area of a triangle we can half the area of a triangle
The area of a triangle = 1⁄2 × base × height

blocks.title: Example 2: Here is a triangle drawn on a centimetre grid. Calculate the area of the triangle.
Example 3: Calculate the area of the triangle.

steps.body:
For the area calculation we use the perpendicular height (it must be straight up, not diagonal).  
The height of this triangle is 12 metres.

Area = 1⁄2 × base × height  
Area = 1⁄2 × 8 × 12  
Area = 4 × 12  
**Area = 48m2**

items.prompt: A triangle has a base of $12$ cm and a perpendicular height of $9$ cm. What is its area?
A triangle has a base of $15$ m, a perpendicular height of $8$ m and a sloping side of $17$ m. What is its area?
items.explanation: Use the perpendicular height, not the sloping side. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 8 = 60\text{ m}^2$.

blocks.text: ### Finding the area of a parallelogram
A parallelogram is a quadrilateral with two sets of parallel sides.
A parallelogram can be made into a rectangle by cutting off and moving a triangle:
The area of a parallelogram = base × height

blocks.title: Example 4: Here is a parallelogram drawn on a centimetre grid. Calculate the area of the parallelogram.
Example 5: Calculate the area of the parallelogram.

steps.body:
For the area calculation we use the perpendicular height (it must be straight up, not diagonal).  
The height of this parallelogram is 11 metres.

Area = base × height  
Area = 8 × 11  
**Area = 88m2**

items.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of $7$ cm and a perpendicular height of $5$ cm. What is its area?
items.explanation: The area of a parallelogram is base × perpendicular height, so $7 \times 5 = 35\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A parallelogram has an area of $96\text{ m}^2$ and a base of $12$ m. What is its perpendicular height?
items.explanation: Since area = base × height, divide the area by the base: $96 \div 12 = 8$ m.

blocks.text: ### Finding the area of a trapezium
The image below shows a trapezium, a trapezium (trapezoid in American English) is a quadrilateral with two parallel sides.

The area of a trapezium = 1⁄2(a + b) × height  
Where a and b are the lengths of the two parallel sides
This formula can be made by splitting the trapezium into a rectangle and a triangle (you don't have to know where the formula comes from, you just have to know the formula).

blocks.title: Example 6: Find the area of the trapezium

steps.body:
For the trapezium above:  
Area = 1⁄2(6 + 10) × 7  
Area = 1⁄2(16) × 7  
Area = 8 × 7  
Area = 56 cm2

items.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of $9$ cm and $15$ cm and a perpendicular height of $6$ cm. What is its area?
A trapezium has an area of $60\text{ cm}^2$ and parallel sides of $8$ cm and $12$ cm. What is its perpendicular height?
items.explanation: Half the sum of the parallel sides is $\frac{1}{2}(8+12)=10$. Therefore $10 \times h=60$, so $h=6$ cm.

blocks.text: The perimeter of a shape is the distance around the edge of the shape
Here is a rectangle drawn on a centimetre grid.
To find the perimeter of a shape we add up the lengths of all of the sides
This rectangle has two sides with a length of 6cm and two sides with a length of 3cm
Perimeter = 6 + 6 + 3 + 3
Perimeter = 18 cm

blocks.title: Example 1: A rectangle is drawn on a centimetre grid Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle
Example 2: Calculate the perimeter of the triangle

items.prompt: A rectangle is $11$ cm long and $4$ cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.explanation: Add all four sides: $11+11+4+4=30$ cm. Equivalently, $2(11+4)=30$ cm.

items.prompt: A square has an area of $49\text{ cm}^2$. What is its perimeter?
items.explanation: The side length is $7$ cm because $7 \times 7=49$. Its perimeter is $4 \times 7=28$ cm.

items.prompt: Two identical rectangles, each $7$ cm by $4$ cm, are joined along one full $4$ cm edge. What is the perimeter of the combined shape?
items.explanation: The two perimeters total $2(7+4)+2(7+4)=44$ cm. The joined $4$ cm edge is inside and was counted twice, so subtract $8$ cm: $44-8=36$ cm.
